However, the traditional recipe for osso buco alla milanese often includes a component called "polenta" or "risotto alla milanese" as a side dish. Risotto is typically made with Arborio rice, which contains gluten. 

But, the main dish itself, the osso buco, is gluten-free. The ingredients used in the sauce, such as veal shanks, vegetables, white wine, and broth, do not contain gluten.

To make osso buco alla milanese gluten-free, you can serve it with a gluten-free side dish, such as sautéed vegetables or a gluten-free polenta made from cornmeal.
